title: Peak Performance: Elevate Your Game, Avoid Burnout, and Thrive with the New Science of Suc
description: What does it take to go from good to great? Step up at work, in sports, and at home with this “transfixing book on how to sustain peak performance and avoid burnout” (Adam Grant). A few common principles drive performance, regardless of the field or the task at hand. Whether someone is trying to qualify for the Olympics, break ground in mathematical theory or craft an artistic masterpiece, many of the practices that lead to great success are the same. In Peak Performance, Brad Stulberg, a former McKinsey and Company consultant and writer who covers health and the science of human performance, and Steve Magness, a performance scientist and coach of Olympic athletes, team up to demystify these practices and demonstrate how you can achieve your best. The first book of its kind, Peak Performance combines the inspiring stories of top performers across a range of capabilities—from athletic to intellectual and artistic—with the latest scientific insights into the cognitive and neurochemical factors that drive performance in all domains. In doing so, Peak Performance uncovers new linkages that hold promise as performance enhancers but have been overlooked in our traditionally- siloed ways of thinking. The result is a life-changing book in which you can learn how to enhance your performance via myriad ways including: optimally alternating between periods of intense work and rest; priming the body and mind for enhanced productivity; and developing and harnessing the power of a self-transcending purpose. In revealing the science of great performance and the stories of great performers across a wide range of capabilities, Peak Performance uncovers the secrets of success, and coaches you on how to use them. If you want to take your game to the next level, whatever "your game" may be

title: A Peak Performance: A Fake Dating, Enemies-to-lovers, Small Town Romance (The Riggs Family
description: Beautiful. Infuriating. Enemy. I’m not the hero. I’m the fun one. The easygoing, youngest Riggs brother who makes people laugh. I’m a good time. Men want to be me. Women just want me. Except one. My new boss. My neighbor. My competition. And now, the woman I’ve just publicly claimed to love. Contessa Costa crashed into my small town and took the job at my family’s company. One that’s supposed to be mine. She’s not the kind of woman who needs rescuing, but when I witnessed the way our biggest competitor, and her ex-husband, talked to her and then touched her, I didn’t have another choice. Now I’m stuck trying to keep up appearances of this “relationship” for a marketing campaign that might be a career-ending gamble. And to prove to my father that I’m the committed and capable choice for CEO. But our lies are starting to feel better than our truth. Now I’m trying to decide if what I want is worth fighting for or if I’d rather just be fighting with her. Rest assured that the book is not mere theory. Ericsson’s research focuses on the real world, and he explains in detail, with examples, how all of us can apply the principles of great performance in our work or in any other part of our lives.”— Fortune Anders Ericsson has made a career studying chess champions, violin virtuosos, star athletes, and memory mavens. Peak distills three decades of myth-shattering research into a powerful learning strategy of deliberate practice that is fundamentally different from the way people traditionally think about skill acquisition. Whether you want to stand out at work, improve your athletic or musical performance, or help your child achieve academic goals, Ericsson’s revolutionary methods will show you how to improve at almost any skill that matters to you. “The science of excellence can be divided into two eras: before Ericsson and after Ericsson. title: Peak Performance (Estate Sale Mysteries Book 2)
cats: Two-Hour Mystery, Thriller & Suspense Short Reads
description: A Vermont ski lodge in January. A dead man in the snow. And somewhere in the attic of Ridgeline Lodge, a hidden invention that someone decided was worth killing over. Callie Vance arrives at Kettle Ridge to liquidate the sprawling mountain estate of Harlan Mabry—engineer, inventor, and the kind of man who built things with his hands and documented everything he made. The job should take two weeks. Then she finds a prototype in a locked workshop, and the man who dies on the mountain wasn't supposed to be there at all. The motive is greed—pure and uncomplicating. But the trail of who knew about Harlan's work, who came to Kettle Ridge to claim it, and who made sure a rival collector wouldn't leave is buried in eight years of records, a workshop full of careful notation, and a community that loved Harlan Mabry and has very strong feelings about what happens to what he left behind. Winston has never worked mountain cold before. His nose adapts. Callie takes notes. And slowly, the shape of what actually happened in that attic starts to hold. Peak Performance is the second book in the Estate Sale Mysteries series—a clean, satisfying cozy with sharp wit, a mountain setting, and a case built piece by careful piece. title: Peak Performance: The Five Principles Every Great Business Lives By (The Pinnacle Series B
description: What if your business could climb higher than you ever imagined? Every great company starts with a dream—of A-players working together, thriving in a strong culture, delivering exceptional results. But somewhere along the way, that dream gets lost in the chaos of growth. In Peak Performance , visionary coach Gregory Cleary reveals the proven system behind dozens of high-value business transformations. Built on five foundational principles—People, Purpose, Playbooks, Performance, and Profits—the Pinnacle Formula helps leaders unlock clarity, build unstoppable teams, and scale with confidence. Cleary goes beyond off-the-shelf operating systems with a flexible, high-impact approach tailored to fast-moving businesses. Inside, you’ll discover: How to attract and retain A-players at every level A smarter way to run meetings that actually drive results Playbooks to streamline execution and reduce decision fatigue Strategies to boost performance and profits—without burning out your team Filled with actionable tools and real-world success stories—from a $400M construction firm to a 100+ location fitness brand— Peak Performance offers a clear roadmap to help your company reach its summit. title: Peak Performance Every Time: Strategies for Confidence, Motivation, and Focus
description: Most people have good days…and not so good days. When they step back and ask what makes the difference, many conclude that it’s that stuff that happens between their ears. So, how do we engineer our mindset? How do we get our mental game right, so that we can perform at our best, consistently? Peak Performance Every Time provides readers with a detailed look into how to build the critical components of a great mental game. It will help them to hone their focus, control their confidence, master motivation and deliver their best ‘under pressure’. In short, it will help deliver peak performance, every time. The book provides a practical guide to performance psychology, based on approaches and methods that have been tried and tested in the demanding world of elite sport. In addition to applied practice, it provides real life examples and case studies from both elite sport and business, plus the underpinning theory and research. This book will be invaluable to anyone trying to reach their full potential, in particular athletes, coaches, managers and executives. It may also be of interest to sports psychology, management and business students.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_1"]', '#CardInstanceP9nUBQi0R0pZgmZPIIHjBA')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_1',{wb: 1})} ._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_icon_core_report__Fs1ah{color:#0f1111;color:var(--aok-sfs-color-page-primary-normal-fg,#0f1111);display:inline-block;-webkit-filter:none;filter:none;-webkit-filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,none);filter:var(--aok-sfs-effect-mode-dark-color-silhouette-white,none);height:20px;margin-right:4px;width:20px}._tell-amazon-desktop_style_tell_amazon_modal_spinner_

title: Peak Performance: The First Welsh Woman to Climb Everest (Quick Reads)
description: 'You fall you're dead,' the voice inside my head told me. I was balancing on a knife-edge ridge, sheer drops either side of me. The cold was chilling me to my core. But I could not give up. I had to focus, The summit was within reach. Everest: the highest mountain in the world and also one of the most dangerous. On May 24 2007, Tori James made history when she became the first Welsh woman, and youngest British woman, to climb to the summit of Everest. It was an amazing achievement for the petite farmer's daughter from Pembrokeshire.
